claim: Etv transcription factors Etv1, Etv4, and Etv5 are controlled by FGF-ERK signaling during lens development.
source: Previous studies have shown that Etv transcription factors are controlled by FGF signaling during embryonic development.
evidence: Supported by genetic ablation experiments showing loss of Etv expression in Fgfr, Mek, and Erk mutants (Figure 1), and by citation to previous work.

claim: Genetic ablation of Fgfr1 and Fgfr2 prevents lens vesicle formation in Pax6Le-Cre; Fgfr1fl/fl; Fgfr2fl/fl embryos.
source: As we and others have previously reported, genetic ablation of FGF receptors prevented the lens ectoderm from forming the lens vesicle in the Pax6Le-Cre; Fgfr1fl/fl; Fgfr2fl/fl (Fgfr CKO) embryo (Figure 1A–H, arrows) (Collins et al., 2018; Garcia et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by histological data in Figure 1 and citations to previous studies.

claim: ERK phosphorylation and expression of Etv1, Etv4, and Etv5 are lost in Fgfr CKO lens ectoderm.
source: Importantly, both ERK phosphorylation and expression of Etv1, Etv4 and Etv5 were also lost in the Fgfr CKO lens ectoderm (Figure 1A–H, outlined), demonstrating that FGF signaling indeed controls ERK and Etv activities during lens induction.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining and in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Deletion of Mek1/2 or Erk1/2 abolishes expression of Etv genes in the lens.
source: Although the lenses were formed in Pax6Le-Cre; Mek1(Map2k1)fl/fl; Mek2(Map2k2)-/- (Mek CKO) and Pax6Le-Cre; Erk1(Mapk3)-/-; Erk2(Mapk1)fl/fl (Erk CKO) embryos, they failed to express any of the Etv genes (Figure 1I–Q, circled).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1I-Q.

claim: Etv1/4/5 deletion reduces lens size at E14.5.
source: In Pax6Le-Cre; Etv1fl/fl; Etv4-/-; Etv5fl/fl embryos (Etv TKO), the lens induction and lens vesicle formation were unaffected, but the lens size was reduced at E14.5 as shown by Hematoxylin and Eosin staining (Figure 2A and E).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2A and E.

claim: Apoptosis increases in the epithelium and transitional zone of Etv TKO lenses.
source: Consistent with this, apoptosis increased in the epithelium and the transitional zone as indicated by TUNEL staining (Figure 2B,F and I, arrows).
evidence: Supported by TUNEL staining data shown in Figure 2B, F, and I.

claim: Proliferation of lens epithelial cells is reduced in Etv TKO mutants.
source: On the other hand, proliferation of the lens epithelial cells was reduced as measured by EdU incorporation assay (Figure 2C,D and I, arrowheads).
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 2C, D, and I.

claim: Etv TKO lenses display ectopic expression of Cyclin D1 in the posterior lens.
source: In contrast, the Etv TKO lens displayed ectopic expression of Cyclin D1 in the posterior lens (Figure 2G, arrow) and persistent EdU- and pHH3-positive cells in the fiber cell compartment (Figure 2C,D,G and H, inserts).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Etv TKO lenses show persistent EdU- and pHH3-positive cells in the fiber cell compartment.
source: In contrast, the Etv TKO lens displayed ectopic expression of Cyclin D1 in the posterior lens (Figure 2G, arrow) and persistent EdU- and pHH3-positive cells in the fiber cell compartment (Figure 2C,D,G and H, inserts).
evidence: Supported by EdU and pHH3 staining data shown in Figure 2C, D, G, and H.

claim: RNA sequencing analysis identified 834 genes with statistically significant changes in expression (p<0.05) in Etv TKO mutants, with 288 genes up-regulated and 283 genes down-regulated by at least two folds.
source: Among the 834 genes showing statistically significant changes in expression (p<0.05), 288 and 283 genes were up- and down-regulated by at least two folds, respectively.
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing analysis of control and Etv TKO transitional zone cells.

claim: Etv genes regulate their own expression.
source: Interestingly, we noticed that the remaining transcripts of three Etv genes were reduced in mutant samples, suggesting that Etv genes regulated their own expressions (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Fgfr1 and Fgfr3 are down-regulated in Etv TKO mutants.
source: The RNA sequencing data indicated that the receptors for FGF signaling, Fgfr1 and Fgfr3, were down-regulated in the Etv TKO mutant (Figure 3C), which were confirmed by RNA in situ hybridization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing data (Figure 3C) and RNA in situ hybridization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Fgfr1 and Fgfr3 double mutant lenses do not exhibit any overt phenotype.
source: Although this suggests a positive feedback regulation of FGF receptors by Etv genes, it is unlikely to affect lens development, because previous studies have shown that Fgfr1 and Fgfr3 double mutant lenses did not exhibit any overt phenotype (Zhao et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study (Zhao et al., 2008).

claim: Spry2 transcript level is reduced in Etv TKO mutant lenses.
source: On the other hand, the transcript level of Spry2, an inhibitor of receptor tyrosine kinases, was also reduced, which we confirmed by RNA in situ hybridization in Etv TKO mutant lenses (Figure 3D and F, arrows).
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing and RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3D and F.

claim: SPRY2 is a direct target of PEA3/ETV family genes.
source: This is consistent with previous ChIP-seq analysis which revealed that SPRY2 is a direct target of PEA3/ETV family genes (Yan et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous ChIP-seq study (Yan et al., 2013).

claim: Spry2 expression is lost in Erk CKO mutants.
source: Since we have shown above that expression of Etv1, Etv4 and Etv5 in the lens is dependent on ERK signaling (Figure 1I–Q), it is not surprising that Spry2 expression is also lost in Erk CKO mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, arrows).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ERK phosphorylation is ectopically activated in Etv TKO mutant lenses.
source: Considering that Sprouty proteins are known to inhibit Ras-MAPK signaling (Hanafusa et al., 2002), this suggests that Etv regulation of Spry constitutes a negative feedback loop to regulate FGF-ERK activity. Indeed, we notice that ERK phosphorylation was ectopically activated in Etv TKO mutant lenses (Figure 3E and G, arrows).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3E and G, and citation to previous work on Sprouty function.

claim: Etv deletion enhances the activity of the MAP kinase pathway.
source: Moreover, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) showed that Etv deletion enhanced the activity of the MAP kinase pathway (Figure 3H), which is known to be decreased in FGF receptor mutants.
evidence: Supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Egr1 and Fos expression increases in Etv TKO mutants.
source: In support of the upregulation of ERK activity, we also observed increasing expression of Egr1 and Fos (Figure 3C), two early response genes for Ras-MAPK signaling.
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Maf protein is still present in Etv TKO mutant lenses.
source: Unexpectedly, immunostaining showed that both Maf and α-crystallins proteins were still present in Etv TKO mutant lenses (Figure 4A,B,F and G).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4A, B, F, and G.

claim: α-crystallin protein is still present in Etv TKO mutant lenses.
source: Unexpectedly, immunostaining showed that both Maf and α-crystallins proteins were still present in Etv TKO mutant lenses (Figure 4A,B,F and G).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4A, B, F, and G.

claim: γA-crystallin expression is not significantly reduced in Etv TKO mutant lenses.
source: Similarly, we did not detect a significant reduction in γA-crystallin expression (Figure 4C and H), which is normally induced after αA-crystallin in more mature lens fiber cells.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4C and H.

claim: Cryaa and Cryga mRNAs are abundantly expressed in Etv TKO lenses.
source: To avoid the possibility that protein perdurance may obscure the dynamic changes in gene expression, we also performed RNA in situ hybridization, which showed abundant expression of Cryaa and Cryga mRNAs in Etv TKO lenses (Figure 4D,E,I and J).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4D, E, I, and J.

claim: There are no statistically significant changes in the transcript levels of Cryaa, Cryga and Maf in Etv TKO RNA sequencing data.
source: Consistent with this, there were no statistically significant changes in the transcript levels of Cryaa, Cryga and Maf in our RNA sequencing data.
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing analysis.

claim: Lens differentiation can proceed in the absence of Etv transcription factors.
source: Based on these results, lens differentiation can apparently proceed in the absence of Etv transcription factors.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that differentiation markers are still expressed in Etv TKO mutants.

claim: Combined deletion of Erk1 and Erk2 results in a drastic reduction in lens size.
source: Indeed, combined deletion of Erk1(Mapk3) and Erk2(Mapk1) resulted in a drastic reduction in lens size as previously reported (Xie et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by histological observations and citation to previous study.

claim: Maf, α- and γ-crystallins mRNA and protein are still expressed in Erk CKO mutant lenses.
source: However, Maf, α- and γ-crystallins mRNA and protein were still expressed in Erk CKO mutant lenses (Figure 4K–O).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining and in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4K-O.

claim: Maf, α- and γ-crystallins staining intensity is not significantly reduced in Mek CKO mutant lenses.
source: In the severely diminished Mek CKO mutant lenses, we again failed to detect significant reduction in the intensity of Maf, α- and γ-crystallins staining (Figure 4P–T).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4P-T.

claim: Genetic ablation of Erk and Etv transcription factors does not abolish lens differentiation as in FGF receptor mutants.
source: Therefore, genetic ablation of Erk and Etv transcription factors did not abolish lens differentiation as in FGF receptor mutants.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of phenotypes across different mutants.

claim: Lens-specific overexpression of Fgf3 in Fgf3OVE391 transgenic animals greatly elevates ERK phosphorylation in the lens.
source: As we and others have previously reported (Collins et al., 2018; Li et al., 2019; Robinson et al., 1998), the lens-specific overexpression of Fgf3 in Fgf3OVE391 transgenic animals greatly elevated ERK phosphorylation in the lens (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5A and B, and citations to previous studies.

claim: Fgf3 overexpression leads to increased expression of Etv1, Etv4, Etv5 and Spry2 in the lens.
source: Consistent with regulation of Etv and Spry2 by ERK signaling we showed above, this led to increased expression of Etv1, Etv4, Etv5 and Spry2 in the Fgf3OVE391 lens (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), which was accompanied by ectopic induction of Maf and γ-crystallin but loss of E-cadherin in Pax6-positive anterior lens epithelium (Figure 5F,J and N, arrows).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Fgf3 overexpression causes ectopic induction of Maf and γ-crystallin but loss of E-cadherin in Pax6-positive anterior lens epithelium.
source: Consistent with regulation of Etv and Spry2 by ERK signaling we showed above, this led to increased expression of Etv1, Etv4, Etv5 and Spry2 in the Fgf3OVE391 lens (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), which was accompanied by ectopic induction of Maf and γ-crystallin but loss of E-cadherin in Pax6-positive anterior lens epithelium (Figure 5F,J and N, arrows).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5F, J, and N.

claim: Pax6Le-Cre;R26EtvEnR lenses are reduced in size like those of Etv TKO mutants.
source: Consistent with this, Pax6Le-Cre;R R26EtvEnR lenses were reduced in size like those of Etv TKO mutants, while the expression of E-cadherin, Maf and γ-crystallin was maintained (Figure 5G,K,O and Q).
evidence: Supported by histological and immunostaining data shown in Figure 5G, K, O, and Q.

claim: Expression of E-cadherin, Maf and γ-crystallin is maintained in Pax6Le-Cre;R26EtvEnR lenses.
source: Consistent with this, Pax6Le-Cre;R R26EtvEnR lenses were reduced in size like those of Etv TKO mutants, while the expression of E-cadherin, Maf and γ-crystallin was maintained (Figure 5G,K,O and Q).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5G, K, O, and Q.

claim: The lens remains smaller in Pax6Le-Cre; Fgf3OVE391; R26EtvEnR mutant than that of the control.
source: After crossing with Fgf3OVE391, the lens remained smaller in the Pax6Le-Cre; Fgf3OVE391; R26EtvEnR mutant than that of the control (Figure 5Q).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5Q.

claim: Expression of Etv1, Etv4, Etv5 and Spry2 in Pax6Le-Cre; Fgf3OVE391; R26EtvEnR mutant is diminished but not abrogated compared to that in Fgf3OVE391.
source: Of note, the expression of Etv1, Etv4, Etv5 and Spry2 in the Pax6Le-Cre; Fgf3OVE391; R26EtvEnR mutant was diminished but not abrogated compared to that in Fgf3OVE391 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggesting that Etv activities was partially inhibited by EtvEnR.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: In Pax6Le-Cre; Fgf3OVE391; R26EtvEnR lenses, Maf and γ-crystallins are restricted to the lens fiber compartment, while E-cadherin is preserved in the anterior lens epithelium.
source: Nevertheless, in sharp contrast to Fgf3OVE391, Maf and γ-crystallins were restricted to the lens fiber compartment in Pax6Le-Cre; Fgf3OVE391; R26EtvEnR lenses, while E-cadherin was preserved in the anterior lens epithelium (Figure 5H,L and P).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5H, L, and P.

claim: Inhibition of Etv transcriptional activities prevents FGF signaling from inducing ectopic expression of fiber-specific genes in the lens epithelium.
source: Therefore, inhibition of Etv transcriptional activities prevented FGF signaling from inducing ectopic expression of the fiber-specific genes in the lens epithelium.
evidence: Inferred from the genetic epistasis experiment comparing Fgf3OVE391 and Pax6Le-Cre; Fgf3OVE391; R26EtvEnR phenotypes.

claim: Etv transcription factors are not essential for normal lens differentiation at the transitional zone, but they are required for FGF signaling to directly convert lens epithelial cells into lens fibers.
source: Taken together, these results showed that Etv transcription factors were not essential for normal lens differentiation at the transitional zone, but they were required for FGF signaling to directly convert lens epithelial cells into lens fibers.
evidence: Inferred from the combined results of loss-of-function and gain-of-function experiments.

claim: The transitional zone marked by the boundary between Foxe3 and Prox1 is moved anteriorly in Etv TKO mutant lenses.
source: Although the fiber cell differentiation genes were still expressed in Etv TKO mutant lenses, we noticed that the transitional zone marked by the boundary between the lens epithelial marker Foxe3 and the fiber cell marker Prox1 was moved anteriorly (Figure 6A and E, arrows).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A and E.

claim: The length of the lens epithelium marked by Pax6 and E-cadherin staining is shortened compared to the circumference of the posterior lens in Etv TKO mutants.
source: As a result, the length of the lens epithelium marked by Pax6 and E-cadherin staining was shortened compared to the circumference of the posterior lens (Figure 6B,F and I, arrows).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 6B, F, and I.

claim: Jag1 protein expression is drastically reduced in Etv TKO mutant lenses.
source: Intriguingly, one of the down-regulated genes in Etv TKO mutants revealed by our transcriptomic analysis was Jag1 (Figure 3C), which encodes the ligand for Notch signaling. By immunostaining, we confirmed that the expression of Jag1 protein was drastically reduced in Etv TKO mutant lenses (Figure 6C and G, arrowheads).
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing data (Figure 3C) and immunostaining data (Figure 6C and G).

claim: Jag1 expressed in lens fiber cells signals to Notch receptors in the lens epithelium to maintain the progenitor pool.
source: Jag1 expressed in the lens fiber cells signals to the Notch receptors in the lens epithelium to maintain the progenitor pool (Jia et al., 2007; Le et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The anterior lens epithelium in Etv TKO mutants exhibits severely diminished staining of Notch1 intracellular domains (Notch1-ICD).
source: In line with the reduced Notch signaling due to Jag1 deficiency, the anterior lens epithelium in Etv TKO mutants exhibited severely diminished staining of the Notch1 intracellular domains (Notch1-ICD), a proteolytic product of Notch1 receptor triggered by Jag1 activation (Figure 6D and H, arrows).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6D and H.

claim: Etv regulates Jag1-Notch signaling to control the timing of lens cell differentiation.
source: These results support that Etv regulates Jag1-Notch signaling to control the timing of lens cell differentiation.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Etv deletion reduces Jag1 and Notch1-ICD expression and shifts the transitional zone anteriorly.

claim: FGF2 induces Jag1 expression in lens epithelial cell culture after 5 hr treatment.
source: By western blot, we showed that Jag1 expression in the lens epithelial cell culture was induced by FGF2 after 5 hr treatment and suppressed by Mek inhibitors U0126 and PD0325901 but not PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (Figure 6J and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6J and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Jag1 expression induced by FGF2 is suppressed by Mek inhibitors U0126 and PD0325901 but not PI3K inhibitor LY294002.
source: By western blot, we showed that Jag1 expression in the lens epithelial cell culture was induced by FGF2 after 5 hr treatment and suppressed by Mek inhibitors U0126 and PD0325901 but not PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (Figure 6J and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6J and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Jag1 expression in the lens is controlled by ERK-mediated FGF signaling.
source: This is consistent with previous reports that Jag1 expression in the lens is controlled by ERK-mediated FGF signaling (Li et al., 2019; Saravanamuthu et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Two Etv-binding sites are located within introns 2 and 5 of Jag1 gene.
source: To determine whether Jag1 is a direct transcriptional target of Etv, we used the recently published ATAC-seq analysis (Zhao et al., 2019) to search the open chromatin regions in the developing lens and identified two Etv-binding sites located within introns 2 and 5 of Jag1 gene (Figure 6K).
evidence: Supported by bioinformatic analysis of ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 6K.

claim: Both introns 2 and 5 sites in Jag1 are occupied by Etv5 in lens cells.
source: By chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), we showed that both introns 2 and 5 sites could be pulled down by Etv5 antibodies but not by IgG control (Figure 6L), demonstrating that these two sites in Jag1 were occupied by Etv in the lens cells.
evidence: Supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 6L.

claim: Jag1 is normally restricted to the nascent lens fibers in wild type control lenses.
source: Jag1 was normally restricted to the nascent lens fibers in wild type control lenses (Figure 5M, arrowheads), but it was abolished in Mek and Erk CKO mutants (Figure 6N and O).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6M.

claim: Jag1 expression is abolished in Mek and Erk CKO mutants.
source: Jag1 was normally restricted to the nascent lens fibers in wild type control lenses (Figure 5M, arrowheads), but it was abolished in Mek and Erk CKO mutants (Figure 6N and O).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6N and O.

claim: In Fgf3OVE391 lenses, Jag1 expression is expanded to the entire lens epithelium at the expense of E-cadherin expression.
source: In Fgf3OVE391 lenses, however, Jag1 expression was expanded to the entire lens epithelium at the expense of E-cadherin expression (Figure 6P, arrow), demonstrating that FGF signaling can induce de novo Jag1 expression in the lens epithelium.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6P.

claim: FGF signaling can induce de novo Jag1 expression in the lens epithelium.
source: In Fgf3OVE391 lenses, however, Jag1 expression was expanded to the entire lens epithelium at the expense of E-cadherin expression (Figure 6P, arrow), demonstrating that FGF signaling can induce de novo Jag1 expression in the lens epithelium.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6P.

claim: Jag1 expression is significantly reduced in Pax6Le-Cre; R26EtvEnR lenses compared to wild-type control.
source: In Pax6Le-Cre; R26EtvEnR lenses, Jag1 expression was significantly reduced compared to those of wild-type control (Figure 6Q, arrowheads), consistent with the role of Etv in Jag1 regulation.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6Q.

claim: Suppression of Etv activity in Pax6Le-Cre; Fgf3OVE391; R26EtvEnR lenses reverses the Fgf3 overexpression phenotype, limiting Jag1 expression domain to the posterior lenses.
source: Suppression of Etv activity in Pax6Le-Cre; Fgf3OVE391; R26EtvEnR lenses reversed the Fgf3 overexpression phenotype, limiting the Jag1 expression domain to the posterior lenses (Figure 6R, arrowheads).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6R.

claim: Etv mediates the FGF-ERK-Notch crosstalk to control the induction of lens differentiation.
source: Based on these results, we conclude that Etv mediates the FGF-ERK-Notch crosstalk to control the induction of lens differentiation.
evidence: Inferred from the combined results showing Etv regulation of Jag1 expression and Notch signaling.

claim: Etv TKO mutants retain nuclei within the lens core, indicating defective organelle clearance.
source: In wild-type control, the maturing fiber cells lost their nuclei as they migrated toward the interior of the lens, eventually forming an organelle free zone (OFZ) (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1, arrowheads). In contrast, Etv TKO mutants retained nuclei within the lens core, indicating defective organelle clearance (Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1, arrowheads).
evidence: Supported by histological data shown in Figure 7A, E, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: RNA sequencing analysis of Etv TKO mutant lenses shows significant down-regulation of Tsc2.
source: Previous studies have shown that inhibition of mTOR signaling accelerated organelle elimination in chick lens explants (Basu et al., 2014). Interestingly, our RNA sequencing analysis of Etv TKO mutant lenses showed significant down-regulation of Tsc2, which forms a heterodimer with Tsc1 to inhibit mTOR activity (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Tsc2 forms a heterodimer with Tsc1 to inhibit mTOR activity.
source: Interestingly, our RNA sequencing analysis of Etv TKO mutant lenses showed significant down-regulation of Tsc2, which forms a heterodimer with Tsc1 to inhibit mTOR activity (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Inhibition of mTOR signaling accelerates organelle elimination in chick lens explants.
source: Previous studies have shown that inhibition of mTOR signaling accelerated organelle elimination in chick lens explants (Basu et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Phospho-mTOR (pmTOR) is localized in the transitional zone of wild-type control lens, but it expands into the fiber cell compartment in Etv TKO mutants.
source: In support of this hypothesis, we observed that phospho-mTOR (pmTOR) was localized in the transitional zone of the wild-type control lens, but it expanded into the fiber cell compartment in Etv TKO mutants (Figure 7B and F, arrowheads).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7B and F.

claim: Etv TKO mutant lenses display significant increase in pS6 and p4EBP1.
source: Similarly, Etv TKO mutant lenses displayed significant increase in pS6 and p4EBP1, two known substrates of mTOR kinase (Figure 7C,D,G and H).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7C, D, G, and H.

claim: pS6 and p4EBP1 are known substrates of mTOR kinase.
source: Similarly, Etv TKO mutant lenses displayed significant increase in pS6 and p4EBP1, two known substrates of mTOR kinase (Figure 7C,D,G and H).
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Inactivation of Etv genes leads to increased mTOR signaling in the lens.
source: Therefore, inactivation of Etv genes led to increased mTOR signaling in the lens.
evidence: Inferred from the observation of increased pmTOR, pS6, and p4EBP1 in Etv TKO mutants.

claim: pmTOR is significantly increased in Tsc1 CKO lenses.
source: To determine whether mTOR activation indeed interfered with nuclei clearance in the lens, we generated Pax6Le-Cre; Tsc1flox/flox (Tsc1 CKO) to ablate the Tsc2 binding partner Tsc1. As expected from the role of Tsc1/2 complex in suppressing mTOR activity, pmTOR was significantly increased in Tsc1 CKO lenses, which also displayed elevated level of pS6 and p4EBP1 (Figure 7J–L).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7J-L.

claim: Tsc1 CKO lenses display elevated level of pS6 and p4EBP1.
source: As expected from the role of Tsc1/2 complex in suppressing mTOR activity, pmTOR was significantly increased in Tsc1 CKO lenses, which also displayed elevated level of pS6 and p4EBP1 (Figure 7J–L).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7J-L.

claim: Nuclei are scattered throughout Tsc1 CKO lenses.
source: Importantly, whereas the wild-type control lens contains a well-defined OFZ in the center, the nuclei were scattered throughout the Tsc1 CKO lenses (Figure 7I and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by histological data shown in Figure 7I and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Etv control of mTOR signaling is required for the terminal differentiation of lens fiber cells.
source: The lack of an OFZ in Tsc1 deficient lenses supports our model that Etv control of mTOR signaling is required for the terminal differentiation of the lens fiber cells.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that both Etv TKO and Tsc1 CKO mutants show similar defects in nuclei clearance and elevated mTOR signaling.

claim: FGF signaling plays important roles during vertebrate lens development.
source: FGF signaling plays important roles during vertebrate lens development.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge and citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: The primary function of FGF signaling is to promote differentiation of lens epithelial cells into fiber cells.
source: As demonstrated by the profound lens defects in FGF receptor mutants, the primary function of FGF signaling is to promote differentiation of the lens epithelial cells into the fiber cells.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge and citations to previous studies.

claim: Deletion of Etv genes causes premature differentiation of lens progenitors as a result of reduced Notch signaling.
source: Contrary to the defective lens differentiation found in FGF signaling mutants, deletion of Etv genes did not prevent the expression of lens fiber genes in normal development. Instead, it caused premature differentiation of the lens progenitors as a result of reduced Notch signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the combined observations of anterior shift of transitional zone, reduced Jag1 and Notch1-ICD expression.

claim: Etv mutations lead to an increase in the activity of ERK and mTOR signaling.
source: Moreover, Etv mutations led to an increase in the activity of ERK and mTOR signaling, with the latter responsible for the abnormal retention of the nuclei in the adult lens.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data showing increased pERK, pmTOR, pS6, and p4EBP1.

claim: Elevated mTOR signaling is responsible for the abnormal retention of nuclei in the adult lens of Etv mutants.
source: Moreover, Etv mutations led to an increase in the activity of ERK and mTOR signaling, with the latter responsible for the abnormal retention of the nuclei in the adult lens.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that both Etv TKO and Tsc1 CKO mutants show similar defects in nuclei clearance and elevated mTOR signaling.

claim: ETV transcription factors activated by FGF signaling can oppose the intended function of the pathway.
source: Therefore, unlike BMP, Hedgehog and Wnt signaling that command their downstream signal-regulated transcription factors (SRTFs) as faithful effectors, ETV transcription factors activated by FGF signaling can oppose the intended function of the pathway.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Etv deletion causes opposite effects compared to FGF receptor deletion in some aspects of lens development.

claim: Deletion of Etv causes significant derangement of ERK signaling.
source: First, deletion of Etv caused significant derangement of ERK signaling, which is the main intracellular pathway activated by FGF.
evidence: Supported by data showing elevated ERK phosphorylation and expression of ERK early response genes in Etv mutants.

claim: Etv-deficient lenses display elevated ERK signaling, which is evident in the increased level of ERK phosphorylation and expression of ERK early response genes Egr1 and Fos.
source: Contrary to the loss of ERK activity in mutants lacking either FGF receptors or downstream mediators Frs2 and Shp2 (Collins et al., 2018; Li et al., 2014; Pan et al., 2010; Zhao et al., 2008), Etv-deficient lenses displayed elevated ERK signaling, which was evident in the increased level of ERK phosphorylation and expression of ERK early response genes Egr1 and Fos.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining and RNA sequencing data.

claim: Elevated ERK signaling in Etv mutants is likely due to reduced expression of ERK inhibitor Spry2.
source: This was likely due to reduced expression of ERK inhibitor Spry2, which has been shown to be a direct transcriptional target of Etv (Yan et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing and in situ hybridization data showing reduced Spry2 expression, and citation to previous ChIP-seq study.

claim: Deletions of Spry genes result in upregulation of ERK signaling in a wide variety of tissues, including the lens.
source: In support of this, deletions of Spry genes have been found to result in upregulation of ERK signaling in a wide variety of tissues, including the lens (Kuracha et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Aberrant ERK activation in Etv mutants may stimulate downstream targets normally silenced by loss of FGF signaling, inducing further compensatory changes that rewire the signaling network.
source: The aberrant ERK activation in Etv mutants may stimulate downstream targets normally silenced by loss of FGF signaling, inducing further compensatory changes that rewire the signaling network.
evidence: Speculative reasoning about the consequences of elevated ERK signaling.

claim: Etv plays an intricate role in stabilizing the intracellular signaling activated by FGF.
source: It underscores the intricate role of Etv in stabilizing the intracellular signaling activated by FGF.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Etv regulates negative feedback through Spry2.

claim: A previous study showed that both lens differentiation genes Maf and Cryaa were under direct control of Etv transcription factors in vitro.
source: This was unexpected because a previous study shown that both lens differentiation genes Maf and Cryaa were under direct control of Etv transcription factors in vitro (Xie et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study.

claim: There is an intrinsic difference between normal differentiation at the lens equator and ectopic differentiation in the lens epithelium.
source: This result suggests an intrinsic difference between normal differentiation at the lens equator and ectopic differentiation in the lens epithelium, which may be shaped by their unique microenvironment and different dosage of FGF signaling.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on the observation that Etv is required for FGF-induced ectopic differentiation but not normal differentiation.

claim: Etv genes are dispensable for FGF-induced cell differentiation under the physiological condition during lens development.
source: Taken together, our results demonstrate that Etv genes are dispensable for FGF-induced cell differentiation under the physiological condition during lens development.
evidence: Inferred from the combined results of loss-of-function experiments in Etv, Erk, and Mek mutants.

claim: FGF plays a dual role in specifying the location of the transitional zone by regulating the timing of lens differentiation.
source: We recently showed that FGF plays a dual role in specifying the location of the transitional zone by regulating the timing of lens differentiation; FGF directly promotes differentiation of lens fiber cells, but it also cooperates with PDGF to restrain differentiation of the lens progenitor cells (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study by the authors.

claim: FGF cooperates with PDGF to restrain differentiation of lens progenitor cells through Jag1-mediated Notch signaling.
source: The latter is mediated by Jag1, which induces Notch signaling in the anterior lens epithelium to suppress progenitor cell differentiation.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study and data in current study.

claim: Jag1 expression is under the direct control of Etv transcription factors and ERK.
source: In the current study, we determined that Jag1 expression is under the direct control of Etv transcription factors and ERK, delineating a complete molecular cascade that connects FGF to Notch signaling.
evidence: Supported by ChIP data showing Etv5 binding to Jag1 regulatory regions and western blot showing ERK-dependent Jag1 induction.

claim: In the absence of Etv, loss of Notch signaling leads to premature differentiation of lens progenitor cells indicated by Foxe3 and Prox1 expression, but the pattern of Crystallin expressions are unchanged.
source: In the absence of Etv, loss of Notch signaling leads to premature differentiation of lens progenitor cells indicated by Foxe3 and Prox1 expression, but the pattern of Crystallin expressions are unchanged.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data showing anterior shift of Foxe3/Prox1 boundary but maintained Crystallin expression.

claim: The terminal differentiation of lens fibers may be slightly delayed relative to onset of progenitor cells differentiation in Etv mutants.
source: This suggests the terminal differentiation of lens fibers may be slightly delayed relative to onset of progenitor cells differentiation.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on the observation of anterior shift of transitional zone but maintained Crystallin expression.

claim: Etv mutants proceed to express Crystallin genes at the comparable level as wild-type controls, which is in sharp contrast to the loss of γ-crystallin expression in FGF receptor mutants.
source: Nevertheless, Etv mutants proceed to express Crystallin genes at the comparable level as wild-type controls, which is in sharp contrast to the loss of γ-crystallin expression in FGF receptor mutants (Zhao et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining and in situ hybridization data, and citation to previous study.

claim: Etv mediates the anti-differentiation function of FGF to activate Notch signaling but it is largely dispensable for the pro-differentiation aspect of FGF signaling.
source: Therefore, Etv mediates the anti-differentiation function of FGF to activate Notch signaling but it is largely dispensable for the pro-differentiation aspect of FGF signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the combined observations that Etv regulates Jag1-Notch signaling but is not required for Crystallin expression.

claim: Etv deficiency augments mTOR phosphorylation.
source: Lastly, our study showed that Etv deficiency augmented mTOR phosphorylation.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data showing increased pmTOR in Etv TKO mutants.

claim: Increased mTOR phosphorylation in Etv mutants is likely caused by reduced expression of Tsc2.
source: This is likely caused by reduced expression of Tsc2, a negative regulator of mTOR.
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing data showing reduced Tsc2 expression in Etv TKO mutants.

claim: Aberrant retention of lens fiber cell nuclei is observed in postnatal Etv mutants.
source: Importantly, we observed aberrant retention of the lens fiber cell nuclei in postnatal Etv mutants, which was mimicked by deletion of Tsc2 partner Tsc1 in the lens.
evidence: Supported by histological data showing persistent nuclei in Etv TKO and Tsc1 CKO lenses.

claim: Deletion of Tsc1 in the lens mimics the aberrant retention of lens fiber cell nuclei observed in Etv mutants.
source: Importantly, we observed aberrant retention of the lens fiber cell nuclei in postnatal Etv mutants, which was mimicked by deletion of Tsc2 partner Tsc1 in the lens.
evidence: Supported by histological data showing persistent nuclei in both Etv TKO and Tsc1 CKO lenses.

claim: Inhibition of mTOR by rapamycin promotes degradation of the organelle in chick lens explants.
source: Previous studies have shown that inhibition of mTOR by rapamycin promotes degradation of the organelle in chick lens explants although the exact mechanism remained controversial (Basu et al., 2014; Morishita and Mizushima, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: This study provides in vivo evidence that mTOR is an important regulator of organelle removal in lens maturation.
source: Our study provides the in vivo evidence that mTOR is indeed an important regulator of organelle removal in lens maturation.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that both Etv TKO and Tsc1 CKO mutants show elevated mTOR signaling and defective nuclei clearance.

claim: This genetic study firmly establishes Etv family transcription factors as SRTFs for FGF signaling in lens development.
source: Taken together, our genetic study firmly establishes Etv family transcription factors as SRTFs for FGF signaling in lens development.
evidence: Inferred from the combined results showing Etv expression is dependent on FGF-ERK signaling and Etv regulates downstream targets.

claim: Etv transcription factors deviate or even oppose the function of FGF-ERK signaling in the lens.
source: Although many SRTFs have proven to be faithful to their upstream signaling, we showed that Etv transcription factors deviate or even oppose the function of FGF-ERK signaling in the lens.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Etv deletion causes opposite effects compared to FGF receptor deletion in some aspects of lens development.

claim: FGF signaling can induce multiple transcription factors, unlike other signaling pathways such as BMP, Hedgehog and Wnt that rely on a single downstream effector.
source: This is likely because, unlike other signaling pathways such as BMP, Hedgehog and Wnt that rely on a single downstream effector, FGF signaling can induce multiple transcription factors.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Diversity among FGF SRTFs may evolve to acquire unique or even opposing functions, which fine tunes the overall transcriptional response.
source: This generates diversity among the FGF SRTFs that may evolve to acquire their unique or even opposing functions, which fine tunes the overall transcriptional response.
evidence: Speculative reasoning about the evolutionary significance of SRTF diversity.

claim: The three PEA3/ETV genes and ERG are the only ETS genes implicated in tumorigenesis.
source: The three PEA3/ETV genes and ERG are the only ETS genes implicated in tumorigenesis, which has been attributed to their ability to mimic the oncogenic effect of Ras signaling (Hollenhorst et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Deletion of Etv transcription factors largely reproduced the phenotype of FGF-ERK mutants in lacrimal gland development.
source: Our previous work in lacrimal gland development has indeed found that deletion of Etv transcription factors largely reproduced the phenotype of FGF-ERK mutants (Garg et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study by the authors.

claim: The functions of Etv deviate considerably from their upstream FGF signaling in the lens.
source: In the lens, however, our current study paints a more complex picture of Etv activity, suggesting that their functions deviate considerably from their upstream FGF signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the combined results showing differences between Etv and FGF receptor mutant phenotypes.

claim: It will be important to elucidate the context-dependent function of SRTFs in development and diseases as transcription factors attract increasing interests as viable therapeutic targets.
source: As transcription factors attract increasing interests as viable therapeutic targets, it will be important to elucidate the context-dependent function of these SRTFs in development and diseases.
evidence: Speculative reasoning about the implications of the study for future research and therapeutic development.
